cohort: The study participants were 991 children with short stature (height <10th percentile) who underwent growth hormone stimulation tests at the Department of Paediatric Endocrinology of the University of Leipzig Medical Center.
finding: GHMax and BMI-SDS were significantly negatively associated in short-statured children, independent of test type.
cross-section timing: Measurements were performed when the children had a mean age of 7.74 years at the time of their growth hormone stimulation tests.
